document.title: On Time-Space Lower Bounds for Finding Short Collisions in Sponge Hash Functions

candidate.title: The Sponge STB Conjecture
candidate.subtitle: Is the short-collision sponge attack optimal for every block bound B >= 2?
candidate.one_line: Whether the Freitag-Ghoshal-Komargodski attack of advantage STB/C + T^2/min(R,C) is optimal for finding B-block sponge collisions in the auxiliary-input random-permutation model, for every B >= 2.
candidate.status_note: Settled only at B ~ T (CDG18) and, for B = 2, in the regime ST^3 <= C (the paper's Theorem 2, recovering FGK22). Open for every other B >= 2. The paper asks for a proof or a refutation and takes no position.
candidate.progress_note: The paper's Theorem 1 gives a new B=1 bound optimal for ST^2 <= C, its Theorem 2 recovers the B=2 bound of FGK22 more simply, and its Theorem 3 proves that the multi-instance technique - the only technique that has produced any of these bounds - cannot prove the conjecture for any B.
risks: The paper prints the conjectured quantity with a bare Theta while every bound and attack it states carries a tilde; the page states it with Theta-tilde and flags the reading.
The paper asks for a proof or a refutation; recording it in the affirmative direction is a reading, flagged on the page.
The attack whose optimality is conjectured is FGK22's, not the source paper's; the page says so.

verify.reason: The conjecture is stated by the paper in its open-problems section, is its own contribution rather than a citation, and is open everywhere except B ~ T. Two defects were repaired: the first draft gave no B=2 regime boundary (the paper's own Theorem 2 settles B=2 when ST^3 <= C), and it presented the conjecture without recording that the paper explicitly asks for a refutation as readily as a proof.

checks.finding: Stated in section 1.3 'Discussions and open problems', p. 8, under the heading 'Is STB-conjecture true for sponge hashing?'.

The paper's own results (Theorems 1-3, sections 3-5) prove B=1 and B=2 bounds and an MI-model limitation; none settles the conjecture, and p. 9 asks for a proof or a refutation. Nothing later in the paper touches it.

The first draft called B=2 wholly open. The paper's Theorem 2 settles B=2 when ST^3 <= C ('the above bound is optimal when the S^2 T^4 / C^2 term doesn't dominate the sum, i.e., ST^3 <= C', p. 4). Corrected: the open case is now stated as B=2 with ST^3 > C, and B >= 3 generally.

B is a function of R and C, not a constant, exactly as the paper's Definition 3 has it; S and T are per the paper's Definition 2; inverse queries are counted, which is the structural difference from the MD setting and is stated.
The conjecture is the source paper's; the attack whose optimality it asserts is FGK22's and the MD conjecture being transported is ACDW20's. Both are attributed on the page and in a dedicated remark.
Sponge, the B-AICR game and the advantage reproduce the paper's section 2.3 and Definitions 2-3 clause for clause, including the initialization (x_0,y_0) = (0,a) and the outer-part exclusive-or.

The first draft omitted that the paper asks for a refutation, which reads as attributing a belief to the authors that they do not state. Corrected by a remark quoting 'either prove or refute' and noting that the sibling open problem, if answered affirmatively, refutes this one for ST^3 > C.
Definitions 1-2 plus the notation list fix the construction, the game, the resources and the asymptotic convention.

corrections.applied: restricted to the regime ST^3 > C, citing the paper's Theorem 2
